transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… I came in because my mind just isn’t holding onto things the way it used to. I’ll sit down to write a simple note for the youth maker program—something I used to do without thinking—and the words and numbers just… scatter on me.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day?
Yes… most days. I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. Even when my wife is being kind, it still feels like I’m… down at the bottom of a well.
Do you feel that you deserve to be punished for something you’ve done?
I… I don’t know. I don’t really think of it that way. I just feel bad, I guess.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed anything like that.
Do you ever get confused about what day it is or where you are?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I know where I am. The days can blur a bit, but I don’t usually get confused like that.
Have these memory problems made you need help with everyday tasks you used to manage on your own?

Yes… some. I’ve let a lot slip. Church things, the garden… the maker program with the kids. My wife and our pastor have had to step in. I don’t really like being alone in the workshop anymore… don’t feel safe there by myself.
Have your memory and thinking problems been steadily getting worse over time?

Yes… it feels like it has. I came in because my mind just doesn’t hold onto things like it used to. Even writing a simple note for the youth maker program… something I used to do without thinking… the words and numbers just sort of scatter on me.
On days when your mood feels a little lighter, does your thinking still seem just as impaired?

Even when I feel a little better… it’s still there. My mind just doesn’t hold onto things like it used to. I’ll sit down to write something simple for the youth maker program, and the words and numbers just… scatter.
Do you believe you have done something terrible that deserves punishment?
I… I don’t know. I don’t think I’ve done something terrible, no. I feel bad about things, but… punishment? I’m not sure.
Have you been having trouble finding the right words when you speak?

Yes… sometimes. It’s like the words are there somewhere, but they don’t come together right. Even writing a simple note for the youth maker program, something I used to do easily… the words and numbers just scatter on me.
Do you believe something bad is going to happen because of something you have done?
I don’t… I don’t really think so. I worry about things, but not like something bad is coming because of something I did.
Do you now need help with basic personal care, like getting dressed or bathing?
I’m… not sure. I can still do those things, I think. It just takes me longer sometimes.
Did your memory problems start after a stroke or another brain illness?
I don’t think so… not that I know of. No one’s told me it was from a stroke or anything like that.
Have you had a seizure?
Not that I know of… I don’t think I’ve had one.
Have you ever gotten lost in a place that used to be familiar to you?
No… I don’t think so. Not that I can remember, anyway.
Has your memory and thinking clearly declined compared with how you used to be?

Yes… it has. I came in because it’s like my mind just won’t hold onto things anymore. Even writing a simple note for the youth maker program—something I used to do without thinking—the words and numbers just sort of scatter on me.
Are you still able to manage your finances on your own?

My wife has been helping more with that sort of thing. I’ve… let a lot slip lately—church responsibilities, the garden, the youth maker program. My wife and pastor have had to step in some, especially with the workshop. I don’t really feel safe being there by myself anymore.
Do your memory and thinking problems keep you from handling things like paying bills on your own?

Yes… I suppose it does. My mind just doesn’t hold onto things like it used to. Even something simple, like writing a note for the youth maker program, I sit there and the numbers and words just… scatter. So bills feel hard to trust myself with.
Did the depression start before the memory problems?
It all seemed to start around the same time… about three weeks ago, after my older sister died. Hard to separate it much more than that.
Before your sister died, had your memory problems already been getting worse for months or years?
No… not for months or years. It’s really just been these last three weeks, since my sister died.

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is most consistent with a severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms, with prominent depressive mood beginning about three weeks after the death of his sister and associated cognitive impairment/pseudodementia-like complaints. Major neurocognitive disorder (F03) is less likely because there is no months-to-years progressive decline, no disorientation, no loss of basic self-care, and onset was acute. Mild cognitive disorder due to known physiological condition (F06.7) is unsupported because the patient denies stroke, seizure, or other known brain illness.
